title: The Prescription Drug $2000 Out-of-Pocket Cap Explained Simply
bigPicture: Starting in 2025, Medicare will limit your yearly prescription drug costs to $2,000.
whatYouNeedToKnow: This cap only applies to Medicare Part D prescription drug plans.
Once you pay $2,000 out-of-pocket, your costs drop to a small copay for the rest of the year.
Only what you pay at the pharmacy counts toward the $2,000. Medicare and your plan payments do not.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Thinking the cap starts in 2024. It begins January 1, 2025.
Counting your monthly premiums toward the cap. Premiums do not count.
actionSteps: Track your out-of-pocket spending using your plan's Explanation of Benefits.
Call your plan or pharmacist to confirm which drugs are covered.
